threads.body: If `_set_embeddings_response_properties(...)` throws (e.g., unexpected SDK response shape), the wrapper will call `invocation.fail(...)` and re-raise, which changes the behavior of the wrapped OpenAI call (instrumentation should not break user code). Make response-property extraction “best effort” (catch and swallow/log extraction errors) and ensure `invocation.stop()` is reliably invoked for successful OpenAI calls (e.g., by separating wrapped-call exceptions from instrumentation/extraction exceptions).

threads.body: `request_model` defaults to an empty string when `model` is missing. That can incorrectly mark the model as “set” (and may produce malformed span/metric attributes or names, e.g., trailing spaces) compared to the previous behavior which omitted the model attribute entirely when absent. Prefer passing `None` (or using `get_value(kwargs.get("model"))`) so “missing model” remains truly unset.

threads.body: The migration intentionally adds `GEN_AI_EMBEDDINGS_DIMENSION_COUNT` to `invocation.metric_attributes` in `create_embedding_invocation(...)` only when `dimensions` is provided in the request. When dimensions are *inferred from the response* (here), the metric attribute is not populated, so metrics may miss the dimension count even though it’s available. Consider also setting `invocation.metric_attributes[GenAIAttributes.GEN_AI_EMBEDDINGS_DIMENSION_COUNT]` when deriving the dimension from the response.

replies.body: Thank you for the suggestion! But I think the `try/except` is the most appropriate solution here as `isinstance` only helps if an attribute is missing or the wrong type and won't save us if a property accessor raises or if a future version changes shape in an unexpected way. I've added `CreateEmbeddingResponse` typing per your above suggestion that I think will mostly address this suggestion.
